newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end weaker, Lion denies takeover rumour.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end weaker, Lion denies takeover rumour.

text.p: * NZ shares pause for breath after rally
* Lion Nathan denies MD Myers selling 16 percent stake
* Big lines in Shortland notes, CDL Hotels
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
335 -5 * NZSC cap index +11.48 at 5,091.37
352 +2 * Volume NZ$45.7 million. Futures up 6 at 1,206
737 -4 * Other movers -9 -15

New Zealand shares ended weaker on Wednesday and brewer Lion Nathan retreated from its morning highs after denying rumours that Chief Executive Douglas Myers was to sell his 16 percent stake to Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Lion ended two cents firmer at $3.52, off its high of $3.65, as the NZSE-40 capital index slipped 8.97 points to 2,399.31.

Rumours swirled in the morning about a full or partial takeover for Lion by Philip Morris. Lion denied Myers was selling down his stake, and a Morris spokeswoman in Sydney said the company was unaware of the rumour.
"When both the company and Philip Morris denied it, it (Lion) came off quite sharply," said Tim Preston, managing director of ANZ Securities.
He said a tie-up between Lion and Morris appeared unlikely, given links betwen Morris subsidiary Miller Brewing and Lion's Australian rival Foster's.
Another broker said: "I really don't see Myers selling out of Lion or selling down." On the other hand, Morris would be an attractive company for Lion to have on its register, he said.
Preston said the wider market was catching its breath after a recent ride higher on fairly thin volume.

Big lines in Shortland convertible notes and CDL Hotels were among the other features. Most leaders declined, with Fletcher Building shedding nine to $4.53 after a very strong run and Carter Holt Harvey easing five to $3.35.
